sprite_blit — GFX2D sprite op

• Data kinds: rgba × rgba → rgba

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.sprite_blit(dst, sprite, x=0, y=0, anchor='top_left', flip_x=False, flip_y=False, opacity=1.0) (implementation को सीधे call करना हो तो import gfx2d; gfx2d.sprite_blit(dst, sprite, x=0, y=0, anchor='top_left', flip_x=False, flip_y=False, opacity=1.0), registry से लेना हो तो opsgfx2d.get("sprite_blit"))

उपयोग

sprite को dst की copy पर integer (x, y) पर composite करता है।

> नीचे का विस्तृत विवरण मूल text में है — सारांश और headings का अनुवाद हो चुका है।

x is the column and y the row of the sprite's anchor point; anchor is one of "top_left", "top_right", "bottom_left", "bottom_right", "center".

Out-of-bounds behaviour is to clip silently, and that is a decision, not an oversight. Half a sprite hanging off the edge of the screen is the normal case in this family, and raising there would make the common path the exceptional one. A sprite entirely outside returns dst unchanged. The contrast with viewport — which raises for the same situation — is

deliberate: a camera asking for pixels that do not exist is a bug in the caller's arithmetic, a sprite walking off screen is not.

x/y must be integers. Sub-pixel placement changes the picture (it resamples), so it is sprite_transform's job and not a silent rounding here.
